panels.title: BAML: the starting reference
panels.note:
Observed medians. Existing batch checks pass; full conformance is unproven.
One HTTP telemetry recording failed validation elsewhere in this collection.

panels.title: The target: beat V8 with telemetry on
panels.note:
Geometric mean = exp(mean(log(BAML median / Node median))). Dashed line is parity.
Adapter + workload + serialization are timed; these are not isolated VM dispatch costs.

panels.title: Where the V8 gap comes from
panels.note:
Ratio of separate medians, 20 processes per configuration. Fixed finite warmup, not proven V8 steady state.
The suite is a chosen reference set, not a claim about every BAML program.

panels.title: Indexed array traversal
panels.note:
Indexing, arithmetic and loop dispatch. No BAML GC observed.
Median of 20 process batch averages; whiskers show observed min–max, not confidence intervals.

panels.title: Merge sort
panels.note:
Handwritten recursion, calls and array copies. No BAML GC observed.
Median of 20 process batch averages; whiskers show observed min–max, not confidence intervals.

panels.title: JSON aggregation
panels.note:
Parsing, strings and aggregate construction. No BAML GC observed.
Median of 20 process batch averages; whiskers show observed min–max, not confidence intervals.

panels.title: Stateful workflow
panels.note:
Persistent state, mutation and eviction. Five BAML collections per batch.
Median of 20 process batch averages; whiskers show observed min–max, not confidence intervals.

panels.title: Generate and sort
panels.note:
Deterministic generation and native numeric sort. No BAML GC observed.
Median of 20 process batch averages; whiskers show observed min–max, not confidence intervals.

panels.title: Workflow CPU cost
panels.note:
Process CPU during the execution batch, including runtime threads. Wall and CPU answer different questions.
Rust is handwritten reference code. All languages include their adapter and output serialization.

panels.title: Memory under allocation pressure
panels.note:
Median of 20 processes; includes adapter, runtime and diagnostics, not just live heap.
BAML collected 8 / 6 times per batch; Node GC coverage is unknown. Collection counts are not a speed score.

panels.title: Telemetry cost stays visible
panels.note:
Drain is a separate post-batch boundary. Recording bytes include preparation and warmup where present.
Small negative low-level overhead is noise, not evidence that enabling telemetry makes BAML faster.

panels.title: Native executable size
panels.note:
Published musl runtime host + bytecode. This measures the LTO / runtime-pruning opportunity, not an AOT result.
WASM size and size without dynamic compilation are unmeasured. Source-file size is not deployment size.

panels.title: Build and startup are separate costs
panels.note:
Workflow build range: 559.702–1,578.407 ms. Bytecode cache off; filesystem caches uncontrolled.
Packed workflow invocation: 8 requests × 64 items, retain 2, sequential 10 ms tools; differs from runtime suite.

panels.title: HTTP at a fixed offered load
panels.note:
Median of trial p99s and throughputs; failures total all five trials. Loopback HTTP/1.1, connection close.
This measures the server + runtime + handler stack. 200 req/s is the test rate, not maximum capacity.

panels.title: Concurrency with waiting
panels.note:
Same tool work in both conditions. Wall includes waiting; CPU does not charge idle wait time.
This does not establish CPU-parallel speedup. True multicore scaling remains unmeasured.

panels.title: MIR → Rust: what to record next
panels.note:
Unmeasured: WASM footprint, dynamic-compiler removal, sustained capacity, GC pause tails and CPU scaling.
Scalar-only MIR → Rust tests cannot yet claim a workflow, GC, JSON or whole-suite win.
